\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\ul\b\fs24 AM\ulnone\b0\par
Commissioner Vargas highlighted various conferences and events that she attended [FAC Conference, New Commissioner Bootcamp, Western Lands Workshop, and Martin County Business Awards December Luncheon]. She thanked The Guardians for their partnership with the Western Lands Workshop. Commissioner Vargas highlighted local award-winning businesses/entrepreneurs from the luncheon. Commissioner Vargas also shared she threw a first pitch for Senior Softball at Langford Park. She provided an update on the New Year's Eve fire at Sand Dune Cafe.\par
\par
Commissioner Capps shared that he attended a dedication for the Habitat for Humanity houses in Pettway Village. He announced he administered the oath to the new Hobe Sound Chamber of Commerce and joined Commissioner Vargas at Langford Park for the first pitch. Commissioner Capps also announced he attended the swearing in ceremony of Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek, Jupiter Island Association Townhall in District 3; and toured Martin County Fire Rescue with District Chief Scott.\par
\par
Vice Chair Ciampi wished all a happy and healthy New Year. He asked for the Board's approval to craft a proclamation for Katherine Steele's Eagle Scout achievement. Vice Chair Ciampi invited residents to attend Dish with the Commish with honorary guest Sandy Thurlow on January 16th at 8 a.m. at Charlie Leighton Community Center. He also invited residents to attend The Patio Playlist (monthly) at the Patio at Palm City Place on January 17th from 6-9 p.m. \par
\par
MOTION: A motion was made by Vice Chair Ciampi, seconded by Commissioner Hetherington, to craft a proclamation for Katherine Steele's Eagle Scout achievement. The motion carried unanimously.\par
\par
Commissioner Hetherington announced that Governor DeSantis approved a conservation easement for over 5800 acres of land at Bull Hammock Ranch through the Rural Family Lands Program. She requested that the Board send a thank you letter to the Governor and the Cabinet. \par
\par
Chair Heard also commented on Bull Hammock Ranch. She suggested that each new Martin CARES class receive a brief presentation from each Commissioner. Chair Heard asked the Board to consider taking over responsibility for the Community Redevelopment Area to increase transparency.\par
\par
Vice Chair Ciampi shared his opinion on Chair Heard's request for consideration of the Community Redevelopment Agency. He stated there should be an increase in information provided to Commissioners versus eliminating local knowledge (CRA). Commissioner Hetherington agreed with Vice Chair Ciampi, highlighting Golden Gate's CRA.\par
\par
\ul\b PM\ulnone\b0\par
Commissioner Vargas requested that the Board consider an item to address the 500 feet buffer at petroleum stations. She addressed holding alternate BOCC meetings to accommodate working residents. Commissioner Vargas spoke about residents concerns to remove signage on major thorough fares in the County; she suggested conducting periodic sweeps. \par
\par
The Board discussed sign regulations and holding BOCC meetings at night. County Attorney Sarah Woods and County Administrator Don Donaldson assisted with Board questions. County Administrator Don Donaldson advised staff will return with an agenda item to discuss zoning changes, the feasibility and fiscal impacts of nightly meetings.\par
\par
\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 The Commissioners each shared and discussed their 2025 priorities.\par
\par
\ul District 1 - Commissioner Vargas\ulnone\par
1. Develop a plan to renovate, surplus, or lease the County Building on Ricou\par
Terrace, in Jensen Beach, for a County benefit.\par
2. Advocate for state and federal funding that funds the preservation of the Florida \par
Wildlife Corridor and any program that identifies and protects Martin County\rquote s \par
western lands for habitat, water quality, sustainable agriculture, and public \par
recreation. \par
3. Advocate for federal funding for construction of the St Lucie Inlet Operation and \par
Maintenance, South Jetty Construction, and Hutchinson Island Shore Protection \par
Project.\par
4. Support State and Federal funding for Water Quality Improvement Grants, Hazard \par
Mitigation Grant Program, and State Revolving Loan Programs.\par
5. Support increased funding for CERP and expedited construction of projects that \par
benefit the St. Lucie River and Estuary.\par
\par
\ul District 2 - Commissioner Hetherington\ulnone\par
1. Secure additional funding and complete Golden Gate El Camino Trail including \par
increased Art In Public Places within the District: CRA and Parks.\par
2. St. Lucie Boulevard Pedestrian Safety Enhancements: a) St. Lucie \par
Boulevard/Jefferson Street intersection stop sign, crosswalk improvements/traffic \par
calming measures (excluding speed tables), and b) complete crosswalk \par
realignment at Sandsprit Park.\par
3. Continue to prioritize Septic-to-Sewer countywide for water quality, complete the \par
Coral Gardens drainage project, secure SRF funds for Coral Gardens S2S, and \par
move the project to bid and construction phase. \par
4. Expand workforce housing opportunities and advocate for environmentally \par
sensitive land conservation, leveraging voter-approved land acquisition funds.\par
5. Reduce or maintain current tax rates and reduce or maintain user fees for \par
recreation facilities.\par
\ul\par
District 3 - Commissioner Capps\par
\ulnone 1. Improving water quality by purchasing conservation lands and converting from \par
septic to sewer.\par
2. Dixie Highway streetscape project in Hobe Sound.\par
3. New fire rescue building at Hobe Sound Beach.\par
4. 714/710 road re-alignment in Indiantown.\par
5. New bridge on County Line Road.\par
\par
\ul District 4 - Chair Heard\ulnone\par
1. Stop overdevelopment in Martin County.\par
2. Acquisition of natural lands component for completion of Indian River Lagoon \par
South.\par
3. Port Salerno Community Redevelopment Area.\par
4. Cease gunfire and illegal activity in Pal Mar.\par
5. Identify spoil sites for placement of 9 million cubic yards of muck dredged from the \par
St. Lucie Estuary and Indian River Lagoon as authorized in IRL South Advance \par
dredging contracts.\par
\par
\ul District 5 - Vice Chair Ciampi \ulnone\par
1. Correct broadband connection issues.\par
2. Begin construction of projects to correct Palm City Farms Drainage/Flooding \par
issues. \par
3. Construct and open a dog park in Palm City. \par
4. Begin construction on the \ldblquote Septic to Sewer\rdblquote conversion project.\par
}

Commissioner Vargas attended legislative sessions in Washington D.C. \par
\par
Commissioner Capps also shared that he attended sessions in Washington D.C. to advocate for Everglades restoration. He thanked staff for their effort and expertise. \par
\par
Vice Chair Ciampi discussed the recent drowning deaths of two children under five. He emphasized the importance of pool safety and ensuring that proper protective measures are in place. Vice Chair Ciampi confirmed the County offers free swimming lessons for children ages 6 months to 17 years old. He extended his heartfelt condolences to the families.\par
\par
Commissioner Hetherington thanked her colleagues for their attendance at the legislative sessions in Washington D.C. She represented the Board at the Larry Pendleton Awards for the Treasure Coast Sports Commission. Commissioner Hetherington recognized audience attendee Sydney Spears [Martin County High School] for being accepted into Girls State.\par
\par

\par
Chair Heard highlighted the recent renovations to the Commission Chambers. She thanked all staff involved in the process.\par
\par
Vice Chair Ciampi wished all a Happy Fourth of July.\par
\par

\b0 Commissioner Vargas presented District 1 2026 priorities.\ulnone\par
1. The County is strategically advancing redevelopment planning for the Ricou \par
Terrace property, working with qualified consultants to evaluate opportunities and \par
innovative approaches for the site. Our focus is to secure the highest and best use \par
that provides clear public benefit, strengthens surrounding commercial activity, \par
and delivers long-term value to Martin County residents.\par
2. Advocate for state and federal funding that will ensure that local tax dollars are \par
leveraged on state and federal priorities that align with the Martin County Forever \par
program.\par
3. Advocate for federal funding for the construction of the St. Lucie Inlet Operation \par
and Maintenance, continuing progress on the South Jetty Reconstruction, and \par
Hutchinson Island Shore Protection Project. \par
4. Support state and federal funding for grants that will support completion of Martin \par
County\rquote s septic-to-sewer projects and stormwater retrofits.\par
5. Support increased state and federal funding for CERP and expedited construction \par
of projects that benefit the St. Lucie River and Estuary, particularly encouraging \par
the Army Corps of Engineers to expedite planning and design of the St. Lucie River \par
Muck Removal Project.\par
\par
\par
\ul Commissioner Hetherington presented District 2 2025 priorities. \ulnone\par
1. Fiscal Responsibility: Reduce or maintain current property tax rates and user fees \par
for public recreation facilities to ensure affordability for residents.\par
2. St. Lucie Boulevard Pedestrian Safety Enhancements: a) implement traffic calming \par
measures along the St. Lucie Boulevard corridor. Enhance crosswalk visibility and \par
install additional safety features. b) Complete crosswalk realignment at Sandsprit \par
Park to improve pedestrian safety.\par
3. Coral Gardens Neighborhood Septic-to-Sewer and Drainage Improvements: a)\par
complete additional drainage improvements, b) ensure timely completion of the \par
sewer project, followed by neighborhood restoration and roadway resurfacing.\par
4. Rail Corridor Quiet Zones: implement Quiet Zones throughout the rail corridor to \par
improve quality of life by reducing train horn noise while maintaining safety \par
standards.\par
\par
\ul Commissioner Capps presented the District 3 2025 priorities. \ulnone\par
1. Improving water quality by purchasing conservation lands and converting from \par
septic to sewer.\par
2. Dixie Highway streetscape project in Hobe Sound.\par
3. New pavilion, fire rescue, and bathroom building at Hobe Sound Beach.\par
4. 714/710 road re-alignment in Indiantown.\par
5. New bridge on County Line Road.\par

\par

2. Acquisition of the natural lands component for completion of Indian River Lagoon \par
South.\par

4. Cease gunfire and illegal activity in Pal Mar.\par

dredging contracts.\par

\par
Kari Driscoll, owner of KW Wrecker Company also addressed the Sheriff's Office tow rotation, she requested revisions to the Sheriff's Office tow rotation manual and reconsideration regarding her company's removal.\par
\par
The following members of the public spoke in opposition to proposed changes to beach regulations that would loosen restrictions on shark fishing near public beaches [PH-2]: Douglas Adler, Robert Wolfe, Jay Noyes, Dottie Lanci, Tom Gion, and Dr. Justin Grubich\par
\par
John Dial spoke regarding the potential fiscal impact of the homestead exemption bill; he urged the County to proactively plan for the potential fiscal impacts. He also requested that the County address ongoing flooding at Mr. Derek Powell's property and nearby development.\par
\par
Darlene Van Riper, Executive Director of the Martin County Taxpayers Association, alleged that the County's information regarding Amendment 3 was misleading. She cited examples of excessive spending that should be included in discussions regarding the amendment's potential fiscal impact.\par
\par
Victoria Blake (Tent City Helpers) requested the County's assistance with providing shelters and services for the unhoused community. She shared personal stories illustrating the challenges unhoused residents face and urged the County to develop a safe, compassionate housing solution.\par
\par
Angela Harrison (Tent City Helpers) proposed the Dignity Buss as a potential overnight shelter for unhoused residents and requested a future agenda item to present the program. She also discussed plans to apply for a $100,000 grant and invited the Board to attend local outreach efforts.\par
\par
Eileen Asselin expressed concerns about the proposed increase in the solid waste assessment. She stated its timing may influence more voters to support Amendment 3.\par
\par

action_text: MOTION: A motion was made by Vice Chair Ciampi, seconded by Commissioner Capps, directing staff to bring forward an agenda item for a one year moratorium on hyperscale data centers to allow legal staff sufficient time to research. The motion carried by the following vote:
minutes_note:
{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\ul\b\fs24 AM\ulnone\b0\par
Chair Heard asked whether the Board was interested in considering a moratorium on data centers. \par
\par
Vice Chair Ciampi shared information about actions taken by other counties and emphasized the need to research the potential benefits and drawbacks of data centers. \par
\par
Commissioner Vargas said she had spoken with a Commissioner from Loudoun County, Virginia, and urged the Board to pause consideration of data centers. \par
\par
Commissioner Hetherington supported further research and requested staff to bring back a presentation concerning Senate Bills 180 and 484. Commissioner Hetherington congratulated Chair Heard and Commissioner Elect Christopher Collins on their election victories and thanked all candidates. \par
\par
Vice Chair Ciampi thanked Commissioner Hetherington for her services and congratulated Chair Heard on her reelection and tenure as Martin County's longest serving commissioner. He commended the other candidates, including Susan O'Rouke, for her commitment to the community beyond the election. Vice Chair Ciampi also acknowledged the passing of Choral Director Ronald L. Corbin. \par
\par
Commissioner Capps acknowledged the passing of Hobe Sound resident and law enforcement officer Mark Budensiek. He congratulated Chair Heard and Commissioner Elect Christopher Collins. He offered encouragement to the other candidates, and discussed the train collision in Hobe Sound. \par
\par
Commissioner Vargas congratulated Chair Heard and Commissioner Elect Christopher Collins, and commended Susan O'rourke. She echoed Commissioner Capps' concerns about railroad crossings, including the crossing in Jensen Beach, and discussed additional lighting and signage along Jensen Beach Boulevard. She also spoke to Supervisor of Elections Vicki Davis regarding voter participation. Commissioner Vargas requested reconsideration of Article 10, citing concerns about information provided by the applicant.\par
\par
\ul\b PM\ulnone\b0\par
Chair Heard thanked residents for their continued confidence in her and congratulated all candidates in this primary season.\par
\par
}

action_text: MOTON: A motion was made by Commissioner Capps, seconded by Vice Chair Ciampi, directing staff to bring back an updated development sign policy, and require developers to have signs printed with appropriate language and require the proposed sign be approved by staff. The motion carried by the following vote:
minutes_note:
{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\ul\b\fs24 AM\ulnone\b0\par
Commissioner Hetherington recognized the strong turnout at the September 11th Remembrance Ceremony at Charlie Leighton Park and the walk over to Veteran's Memorial Park. She expressed hope that the community will move forward in a spirit of unity.\par
\par
Vice Chair Ciampi echoed Commissioner Hetherington's comments and noted that approximately 3000 people participated in the walk. He thanked PAL, Martin County Fire Rescue, and Martin County Sheriff's Office for their efforts. He also recognized The House of Hope's record breaking, 400 foot Cuban sandwich event at Justin Wilson Park. Vice Chair Ciampi extended birthday wishes Sarah [Derek Powell's wife] and recognized his 35th wedding anniversary and his parents' 66th wedding anniversary.\par
\par
Chair Heard thanked the Fire Department and Sheriff's Office for their contributions to the 9/11 ceremony. She recognized a sixth grade student's electric guitar performance of The Star-Spangle Banner and invited him to perform at a Board meeting. She discussed water quality improvements made over the past two years, including muck removal and burning activities at Lake Okeechobee by the SFWMD and FWC. Chair Heard also referenced a discussion with Nick Musia regarding their project to remove phosphorus from the lake and the ribbon cutting ceremony for the C23 and C44 interconnect pump station. She also referenced Governor Desantis' statements regarding $10 billion invested in water quality improvements.\par
\par
Commissioner Capps highlighted the 9/11 Bridge Walk and encouraged residents to participate. He also discussed the yellow roadway signs announcing developments and requested stronger language identifying developments mandated by the State, such as the Baron Landings and Cove Road projects. He suggested language identifying state mandated, administratively approved projects, and state authorized agricultural enclaves.\par
\par
Commissioner Vargas expressed concerns regarding drivers' ability to safely read development signs and supported clearer information. She reported attending the 9/11 bridge walk and pump station ribbon cutting ceremonies. Commissioner Vargas encouraged residents to attend the 5:05 budget public hearing.\par
\par
\ul\b PM\ulnone\b0\par
None were heard.\par
\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Kelly Ribaudo reiterated concerns regarding school zone protections at Citrus Grove Elementary, citing increased traffic and crashes. She urged the Board to reevaluate traffic conditions and consider additional school zone safety measures, including traffic lights.\par
\par
Alexia Haass shared a personal experience involving her four year old child and urged the Board to reduce the 45 mph speed limit near Citrus Grove to improve safety.\par
\par
Iris Haass, accompanied by his daughter Coral, addressed the school zone safety at Citrus Grove and noted that other schools along major roadways have lower speed limits.\par
\par
Stan Kelner, drawing on his experience as a trauma anesthesiologist, emphasized the serious consequences of traffic related injuries and urged the Board to address the school zone safety concerns.\par
\par
Gary Ehrler addressed the September 25th Martin County BOCC meeting and the public comment policy regarding an Article 10 appeal. He stated that the Chair invited public comment but the County Attorney denied it. He also raised concerns regarding transparency and stated that the exchange had been removed from the meeting video.\par
\par
Andrea Horst described witnessing a near collision and urged the Boards to provide school zone signage, crossing guards, and law enforcement presence.\par
\par
Kendall George addressed near collisions at Citrus Grove and asked the Boards to consider measures to improve traffic safety.\par
\par
Christian Milanes, a Citrus Grove parent, expressed concerns regarding traffic safety and spoke in support of establishing a school zone.\par
\par
Erik Barnes urged the Boards to be proactive in planning for growth and protecting children at the Citrus Grove school crossing.\par
\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\ul\b\fs24 IV. Agenda Items\ulnone\b0\par
\par
\ul\b A. County Public Works Projects\ulnone\b0\par
Martin County Capital Projects Administrator Keith Baker presented updates on the Dixie Multi-modal Pathway, Countyline Road Bridge replacement, Port Salerno Resurfacing, Kanner Highway and Lox Road turn lane, and Dixie Highway.\par
\par
City of Stuart Commissioner Sean Reed inquired about project funding sources. \par
\par
Commissioner Blake Capps inquired about the light at Crossrip Street in Hobe Sound.\par
\par
Public Works Environmental Resource Administrator John Maehl presented updates on Martin County Forever acquisitions, dredge spoil site donation, CERP IRL South Estuary restoration, and seagrass restoration.\par
\par
\ul\b B. City Utilities and Engineering Projects\ulnone\b0\par
City of Stuart Director of Engineering and Utilities Peter Kunen presented project updates on the courtesy dock replacement, North Stuart Pump station, and watermain reclamation project.\par
\par
\ul\b C. Village Utilities and Public Works Update\ulnone\b0\par
Village of Indiantown Utilities and Public Works Director Patrick Nolan presented the Village of Indiantown's public works, water, special water, and wastewater project updates.\par
\par
\ul\b D. School District Facilities Capital Projects Update\ulnone\b0\par
Martin County School District Director of Facilities and Planning Mark Sechrist presented the School District's project updates for Murray Middle School's building replacement.\par
\par
\ul\b E. Pre-K Programs Overview\ulnone\b0\par
Martin County School District Principal of Pre-K Programs Angie Gilbride presented an overview of the School District's Pre-K programs.\par
\par
\ul\b F. County / Village Growth and Development Updates\ulnone\b0\par
Martin County Growth Management Principal Planner Samantha Lovelady presented the County's growth and development report.\par
\par
Village of Indiantown Interim Village Manager Michael Giardino provided an overview of projects and progress in the Village of Indiantown. \par
\par
Village of Indiantown's Office Coordinator Lucia Mendoza presented the Village of Indiantown's development activity update.\par
\par
\ul\b Board Comments\ulnone\b0\par
School Board Member Amy Pritchett thanked the Canopy Creek residents for sharing their concerns and asked what actions the School District and County could take to address them.\par
\par
Martin County Vice Chair Ciampi discussed requirements for implementing traffic safety measures. He noted a proposed traffic signal at Newfield and meetings with the Sheriff's Office regarding increased law enforcement presence and enforcement. \par
\par
School Board Vice Chair Dr. Brian Moriarty thanked the residents and expressed dissatisfaction with the response to their concerns. He urged action, requested that any available traffic studies be presented and encouraged the County to address the issue. \par
\par
Martin County Vice Chair Ciampi confirmed that the matter had been presented to the County and requested that the same presentation be provided to the School District. School Member Marsha Powers suggested scheduling a staff presentation for the November meeting or a workshop.\par
\par
Village of Indiantown Council Member Janet Hernandez asked how the School District tracks the progress of residential growth. School Board Chair Marsha Powers responded.\par
\par
City of Stuart Commissioner Merrit Matheson relayed residents' concerns regarding access to Stuart Middle School and the Boys and Girls Club, requesting review of the Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd entrance rather than the rear entrance. He also discussed complaints regarding the school car line operations, including a preference to use Georgia Avenue and concerns that intermittent traffic monitoring was contributing to congestion. Additionally, Commissioner Matheson relayed concerns regarding the need for longer boat trailer parking spaces at Charlie Leighton Park. \par
\par
Martin County Vice Chair Ciampi discussed improvements underway at Charlie Leighton Park, including plans for 48 foot parking spaces to accommodate an average length of 45 feet. He noted that the improvements were being addressed within the site's limitations.\par
\par
School Board Chair Marsha Powers addressed Commissioner Matheson's concerns, she stated that the Boys and Girls Club at Stuart Middle School had agreed to close the rear gate and indicated that the matter would be verified and any necessary corrections made. She also suggested referring traffic concerns involving Georgia Avenue and Ocean Boulevard to the Sheriff's Office.\par
\par
Martin County Commissioner Hetherington noted that this would be her last joint meeting and expressed appreciation for the opportunity to serve the community where she was born and raised. She reflected on accomplishments guided by District 2 residents and expressed her intention to remain engaged as a resident. Commissioner Hetherington thanked staff for their professionalism and expressed appreciation to her colleagues and all of the Boards.\par
\par
\par
\par
\par
\par
}

Commissioner Elect Christopher Collins commended the Board for considering a moratorium on hyperscale data centers and urged the Board to prevent such facilities from locating in the County. \par
\par
Alexander Cooke addressed hyperscale data centers. \par
\par
Linda Smith, representing the Sierra Club Loxahatchee Group, urged approval of Item PH-1 and expressed opposition to data centers in the County. She also discussed the abrupt suspension of MARTY services and advocated for a pay as you throw model for waste reduction.\par
\par
Nicolas Moleiro Heeren discussed hardships associated with his brother's property, including approximately $1.5 million in code enforcement fines related to violations attributed to the previous owner. He requested changes to allow fine reductions for the owners who did not cause the violation.\par
\par
Susan Heeren Malzoni requested that the Board consider modifying the applicable rules to give special magistrates greater discretion to reduce fines. She stated that the property had violations dating back approximately 17 years and urged relief for families facing similar circumstances. \par
\par
Joseph "Joe" Gilio, an Environmental Consultant representing Mr. Moleiro, discussed permitting and compliance issues affecting the property, including dredge and fill permit requirements and PAMP implementation.\par
\par
Roderick Moleiro discussed Section 1.98.B concerning code enforcement liens, un-permitted pond dredging, approximately $1.5 million in fines, and his efforts to bring the property into compliance. He requested an amendment that would allow his case to qualify for relief. \par
\par
Carl Casper supported an amendment to address Mr. Moleiro's situation and reduce undue burdens on property owners facing similar circumstances. \par
\par
Commissioner Capps asked the County Attorney about available remedies for Mr. Moleiro and the history of the applicable policy.\par
\par
County Attorney Elysse Elder explained that an amendment creating an exception for an individual case could raise equal protection concerns. She discussed a uniform approach that would provide special magistrates discretion to reduce fines.\par
\par
Chair Heard addressed historical code compliance issues and stated that the code enforcement process had worked to date.\par
\par
Vice Chair Ciampi stated he had discussed the matter with Mr. Moleiro and Attorney Tyson Waters. He described the circumstances as unique and supported exploring assistance while avoiding preferential treatment.\par
\par
Commissioner Capps suggested a future agenda item to review the history and effectiveness of the code enforcement process, noting the discussion would also benefit newly elected Commissioners.\par
\par
MOTION: A motion was made by Vice Chair Ciampi, directing staff to review information received, and bring forward a policy that gives the magistrate authority and or flexibility to change a fine to zero if the case warrants it. The motion failed for the lack of a second.\par
\par
MOTION: A motion was made by Commissioner Capps, seconded by Commissioner Vargas, to bring forward a future agenda item and discussion on the matter. The motion carried unanimously.\par
\par
Erik Barnes, a parent residing near Canopy Creek, urged the Board to act promptly to improve the school crossing and establish a reduced speed school zone before a tragedy occurs.\par
\par
Kimberly Caldwell Blazie expressed opposition to a proposed rezoning and development to parcel A091-002 in Port Salerno and raised concerns regarding a brownfield.\par
\par
Andrea Horst requested a school zone near Canopy Creek, noting the existing 45 mph speed limit. She stated that a traffic signal alone would not provide sufficient protection and advocated flashing lights and a reduced speed limit. She invited Board members to observe students walking to school in the early morning darkness.\par
\par
Kendal George spoke on behalf of Kelly Ribaudo and as a Canopy Creek parent. She referenced a prior meeting concerning the Board's authority to establish a school zone and Commissioner Ciampi's vote to retain existing conditions. She asked which rules, laws, or ordinances prevented establishing a school zone and stated that she had not observed an increased law enforcement presence. \par
\par
Gail Goldy thanked Commissioner Vargas for addressing the parking concerns at Sandsprit Park and noted that barriers had been installed. She raised concerns regarding vehicles obstructing sidewalks and accessibility for residents. She also urged approval of Item PH-1.\par
\par
Vera Casselbury discussed the potential impacts of data centers on the local community.\line\par
Kay Seely expressed concerns regarding proposed hyperscale data centers within approximately three miles of her home and supported a moratorium. \par
\par
Scott Butler supported a moratorium to allow additional research and expressed opposition to data centers in the County.\par
\par
John Dial thanked the Commissioners for their proactive approach and emphasized the importance of honoring commitments. He asked the Board consider approval of PH-1 and oppose data centers. He also referenced concerns raised by Kimberly Caldwell Blazie regarding a century old banyan tree on the Port Salerno property. \par
\par
Jim Moir, representing Waterkeepers of Florida and Indian Riverkeeper, requested approval of the moratorium.\par
\par
T.C. Ducasse discussed flock cameras and referenced Sheriff's Office records concerning their purchase and use for searches. He raised privacy concerns and requested that cameras be banned and removed.\par
\par
Sergei Kelly opposed data centers and urged the Board to follow staff's recommendation for PHQJ-1.\par
\par
Joe Flanagan discussed Project Graduation's efforts to keep graduating seniors safe. He thanked the Board for its support and presented certificates to the Commissioners.\par
\par
Gary Ehrler reiterated concerns raised by Kimberly Caldwell Blazie regarding banyan and ficus trees and the preservation of green space on small lots. \par
\par
James Martin, identifying himself as a candidate for federal office, expressed opposition to data centers.\par
\par
Ann Vandersteel discussed potential data center sites in Indiantown. She also raised concerns regarding flock cameras and requested oversight from an independent third party selected by the state.\par
\par
Maureen Steele spoke in opposition to data centers.\par
\par
